name: Asakusabashi
tagline: Tokyo in 11 minutes and Otemachi in 13 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Taito City, where JR East and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 13 minutes to Otemachi, 21 minutes to Shinjuku, 31 minutes to Shibuya and 23 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands 3.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 3.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.1 m to 3.9 m, a difference of 2.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 0.5 to 3 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 6 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: ライフ 神田和泉町店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 22 clinics and 29 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 東京自動車連合健康保険組合柳橋病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 三井記念病院, about 11 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) run through it. Toei Asakusa Line also call here. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) runs at 151% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 錦糸町→両国, which this station is not on. Toei Asakusa Line runs at 123%. Its busiest stretch is 本所吾妻橋→浅草, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥130,000 to ¥140,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥260,000 to ¥270,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. plenty of places to eat out pushes the figure up. On the other side, a large projected flood depth holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Bakurocho; for lower rent, Asakusabashi.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Asakusabashi. Bakurocho also has the JR Sobu Main Line and Toei Shinjuku Line, which Asakusabashi does not. With more lines, Bakurocho is the better connected of the two. To Tokyo, for instance, Bakurocho is 7 minutes quicker. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥6,000 more at Bakurocho.

neighbours.lead: Asakusabashi is ahead on how close the centre is and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Asakusabashi. Kuramae has the Toei Oedo Line and Toei Asakusa Line, a different set from Asakusabashi. To Shinjuku, for instance, Kuramae takes 6 minutes longer. On how easy the shopping is, Asakusabashi comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: 江戸通り (3 lanes each way) runs right beside the station. Traffic on it never stops, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 14 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
